title: Linda's Great Burgers
industry_source_label: Restaurant, Food & Beverage / Fast Food Chain
fit_question: Tell me about a time you led a team through a complex challenge. Tell me about a challenge where you had to make risk decisions.
prompt: Linda's Great Burgers is a global burger chain using individual franchises. Believing its market is saturated, it is considering acquiring Heavenly Donuts, a young global coffee-and-donut chain using territorial franchises. Determine whether Heavenly Donuts is a good acquisition and strategic match.
interviewer_notes: Acquisition case with structured synergy brainstorming, exhibit interpretation and a growth calculation. The title page labels it candidate-driven, while the detailed case page labels it interviewer-led; format follows the detailed case page. A final deal decision must remain conditional because purchase price, valuation and integration costs are not provided.

suggested_framework.summary: Assess donut-market attractiveness, Heavenly Donuts, deal returns and strategic fit and synergies with Great Burgers.

children.label: Target revenue, profit, footprint and franchise model
Purchase price, financing and standalone value
Synergy value, integration cost, NPV and return
Management, culture, franchisees and integration risk

stages.interviewer_asks: How would you decide whether Heavenly Donuts is a good acquisition?
stages.expected_answer: Assess donut-market growth and competition, Heavenly Donuts' financial and operating health, purchase price and returns, revenue and cost synergies, franchise-model and geographic fit, management and culture, and integration risks.

stages.interviewer_asks: What does Exhibit 1 tell you, and where are the synergies?
stages.expected_answer: Heavenly Donuts is concentrated in North America, with only 20 European stores and none in Asia or other regions, while Great Burgers has a much broader network. Great Burgers can accelerate geographic expansion, localize market entry, cross-sell or colocate, consolidate procurement, property/equipment and SG&A, and transfer stronger franchise and store operations. Risks include different franchise models and Heavenly Donuts' below-industry sales per store.
good_answer_signals: Finds both revenue and cost synergies
Notes target underperformance and geographic whitespace

stages.interviewer_asks: If Heavenly Donuts must double market share in five years and market size and store count stay constant, what revenue per store is required?
stages.expected_answer: Revenue must double from $700M to $1.4B. Across 1,020 stores, required revenue per store is $1.3725M versus $686K today. Doubling over five years requires a 14.87% revenue CAGR.
good_answer_signals: Calculates about 15% CAGR and challenges assumptions

stages.interviewer_asks: How could the combined company produce that growth?
stages.expected_answer: Expand into Great Burgers' European and Asian footprint, colocate or cross-sell breakfast and snack occasions, improve franchisee selection and operations, add products and healthier options, use loyalty and pricing, and improve marketing while protecting brand differentiation.

stages.interviewer_asks: Should Great Burgers acquire Heavenly Donuts?
stages.expected_answer: Proceed to valuation and diligence because the strategic fit and synergies are promising: broad geographic whitespace, complementary occasions, operating transfer and procurement/property/SG&A savings. But approve the deal only if purchase price plus integration costs are below standalone and synergy value and if roughly 15% annual growth is credible after testing demand, franchisees and culture.
good_answer_signals: Connects growth and synergies to valuation and risk

exhibits.title: Great Burgers and Heavenly Donuts Comparison
exhibits.description: Store footprint, growth, sales, parent revenue, cost ratios and sales-per-store performance for both companies.
exhibits.key_insight: Great Burgers offers geographic and operating capabilities that can address Heavenly Donuts' narrow footprint and below-industry sales per store.

math.question: What per-store revenue and CAGR would double Heavenly Donuts' market share in five years?
givens: Constant total market and store count
math.answer: $1.37M revenue per store and approximately 14.9% annual growth

synthesis: Advance Heavenly Donuts to valuation and diligence, but do not approve without a price. Great Burgers can unlock international expansion, colocations, operational improvement and procurement/property/SG&A synergies. Doubling share with fixed market size and stores requires $1.37M per store and 14.9% annual growth. Buy only if that plan is credible and total price plus integration cost is below standalone and synergy value.
what_great_looks_like: Finds geographic, revenue and cost synergies
Keeps the acquisition decision conditional on valuation
common_pitfalls: Treats every cost-ratio difference as an automatic synergy
Assumes market size and store count will stay fixed without challenge

extraction.notes: The exhibit is candidate-facing and contains inputs only. The source conflicts on format: the title page says candidate-driven and the detailed page says interviewer-led; the latter is used. Reviewed and accepted by Claude 2026-09-30.
